text:
Noah Dobson hasn't scored in 17 games this season, and Montreal keeps winning anyway. He has eight assists, five of them in his last five games, and CBS Sports noted he's picking up the pace.

The goal will come. He has 2.6 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and 37 shots, a normal season's worth of looks for a defenseman, with nothing to show for it. The Canadiens have 53% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, slightly better than without him.

The questions about Dobson have always been defensive, and Evolving-Hockey's numbers from last season still back them: opponents got more chances with him on the ice (bottom 5% of defensemen) while he faced the other team's best (95th percentile competition). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that he shoots a lot but from the outside more than his volume suggests. He's 26 and playing 21 minutes a night for a team near the top of the East. Our projection sees about 41 points.
